newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lull seen for German coffee, consumers covered.
newsitem.headline: Lull seen for German coffee, consumers covered.

text.p: Germany's physical coffee markets were subdued again after price falls last week brought some roaster buying, traders said.
"The industry is taking a break because it is quite well covered for now," one said.
"This pause could last until the Brazilian winter season has ended, by which time consumers hope futures and differentials will have dropped sharply."
Nearby sales were strongly discouraged by the heavy premium of July and September arabicas over the December contract, which closed at 186.00, 164.10, and 151.00 cents/lb last Friday respectively.
Interest last week focused on Central Americans, Colombians and Brazils for July/August 1997 shipment as well as other dates in the second half of the year.
Price fights in the retail market were continuing.
Discounters were raising prices along the lines of the moves earlier this year by established roasters, which each have added around 2.50 marks on average per 0.5 kilo in 1997.
Traders said there were now some signs of backtracking, with roasters trying to lure shoppers with special offers.
Coffee-drinking declines seasonally in the summer months.

El Salvador arabicas of the c.st. grade cost $197 per 50 kg fob, and Colombia excelso was at $195, both down $6 each on the week, with Brazils for Sept at $155, off $4, basis second hand. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
